name: South Okanagan Conservation Fund
summary: A local fund in British Columbia's South Okanagan for conservation projects that reduce a known threat to biodiversity. Registered non-profits apply in an annual call; land acquisition or covenant proposals are accepted all year.
reporting: Interim and final written reports, plus a 10-minute presentation on outcomes each year.

steps: Application by email or hard copy

eligibility.rule: For general projects, be a registered charity or partner with one
For general projects, locate the project within the listed RDOS service area
For general projects, address at least one listed IUCN threat to a biodiversity target
Not government duties, operating-only, recreation-only, infrastructure, lobbying or wildlife feeding projects
Multi-year projects run at most 3 years, with a new application each year
For acquisition projects, support the purchase price with a current appraisal

documents: Interim Progress Report, if continuing a multi-year project

status.quote: Land Acquisition/Securement Projects are always OPEN

applicant_types.quote: Proponents must be a registered not-for-profit organization, or organizations may partner with a qualified organization.

geography.quote: Projects must be delivered in the fund service area which includes RDOS electoral areas

access.quote: Proponents must be non-profit, have registered society status or must partner with an organization that has registered society status.

window.quote: Annual Timeline August to October - Call For Proposals

reporting.quote: Proponents must be prepared to make a 10 minute presentation on the outcomes of their work on an annual basis, in addition to submitting a written interim, and final report.

effort.quote: Applications are to be submitted electronically via email to: socf.meads@gmail.com or, hard copy to: C/O RDOS 101 Martin St. Penticton BC V2A 5J9
December - Review by Technical Advisory Committee
January – RDOS Board of Director’s Final Approval

eligibility.quote: Only registered charities or organizations partnered with registered charities are eligible to apply.
Project falls within electoral areas A, C, D, E, F, I or Summerland, Penticton, Oliver or Osoyoos
Project addresses International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) threats to biodiversity targets, specifically at least one of the following:

The following types of projects will not be considered for funding: (a) Existing federal, provincial, or local government responsibilities; (b) Capacity building or operating only expenses for organizations; (c) Projects with recreational benefits only; (d) Community infrastructure services; (e) Lobbying or advocacy initiatives; (f) Wildlife feeding programs;
Multi-year projects are acceptable to a maximum three years – however proponents must apply each year.
SOCF only funds acquisition projects with a purchase price supported by a current appraisal.

after_award.quote: Proponents must be prepared to make a 10 minute presentation on the outcomes of their work on an annual basis, in addition to submitting a written interim, and final report.

documents.quote: Completed Excel Budget (using the official SOCF template) Project Location Map(s) (JPEG, PDF, or KMZ format) High-Resolution Project Photo (JPEG format for communication purposes) Letter(s) of Support (from primary partner and/or landowner/manager)
Interim Progress Report (Required only for continuing multi-year projects)
